CHAPTER 13 — वर्षर्तुवर्णनम् (VARSHARTTU-VARNANAM)

Introduction — ऋतुवर्णनम् in Sanskrit Kavya (काव्ये ऋतुवर्णनपरम्परा)

Sanskrit poets have always been great lovers of nature. The description of nature (प्रकृतिवर्णनम्) — mountains, rivers, forests, the sky, and above all the six seasons (षड् ऋतवः) — is a defining ornament of classical काव्य. The Indian year is traditionally divided into six seasons: वसन्तः (spring), ग्रीष्मः (summer), वर्षा (the rains, traditionally the months श्रावण and भाद्रपद), शरद् (autumn), हेमन्तः (early winter) and शिशिरः (late winter). Of these, none stirred the poets' imagination more than वर्षा — the season of dark thundering clouds (मेघाः), flashing lightning (तडित्, विद्युत्), dancing peacocks (मयूराः), overflowing rivers (नद्यः) and rejoicing farmers (कृषकाः). The greatest of Sanskrit poets, महाकविः कालिदासः, devoted an entire lyric poem — the ऋतुसंहारम् — to the six seasons (its SECOND canto describes वर्षा), and built his most beloved lyric, the मेघदूतम् ('The Cloud Messenger', a खण्डकाव्य/गीतिकाव्य in the मन्दाक्रान्ता metre), upon a single monsoon cloud seen on the first day of the month आषाढ. In this lesson (NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit, Course 309) we read an original descriptive prose passage on the monsoon, then study four famous public-domain verses on वर्षा — one from the ऋतुसंहार, two from the मेघदूत, and one celebrated अन्योक्ति on the चातक bird traditionally ascribed to भर्तृहरि (नीतिशतकम्) — each with शब्दार्थ (word meanings), अन्वय (prose order) and English translation. Finally we draw senior-secondary grammar from the texts: सन्धि, समास (especially the picture-packing descriptive compounds of वर्णन-poetry), विभक्ति and कृदन्त forms.

गद्यम् — वर्षावर्णनम् (An original descriptive prose passage)

वर्षाकालः समागतः। गगने सर्वत्र नीलाः मेघाः गर्जन्ति। तडित् क्षणं क्षणं चमकति। शीतलः वायुः वहति। महती वृष्टिः भवति। वृष्टेः जलेन वसुधा हरिता जाता। वनेषु मयूराः केकारवं कृत्वा आनन्देन नृत्यन्ति। चातकाः वृष्टिजलं पातुं गगनं पश्यन्ति। नद्यः जलपूर्णाः भूत्वा वेगेन वहन्ति। तडागाः कूपाः च जलेन पूर्णाः भवन्ति। कृषकाः प्रसन्नाः सन्तः क्षेत्रेषु हलैः कृषित्वा बीजानि वपन्ति। ते गायन्तः कार्यं कुर्वन्ति। बालकाः वृष्टौ क्रीडन्ति। सर्वा प्रकृतिः नवजीवनं प्राप्नोति। अतः एव कवयः वर्षर्तुं 'जीवनदाता' इति वदन्ति।

शब्दार्थ: समागतः = has arrived; गगने = in the sky; गर्जन्ति = (they) thunder; तडित् = lightning; चमकति = flashes; वृष्टिः = rain; वसुधा = the earth; हरिता = green; केकारवम् = the cry of the peacock; नृत्यन्ति = (they) dance; चातकाः = chataka birds (by poetic convention they drink only raindrops); पातुम् = to drink; जलपूर्णाः = full of water; वेगेन = swiftly; तडागाः = ponds; कूपाः = wells; कृषकाः = farmers; हलैः = with ploughs; कृषित्वा = having ploughed; बीजानि = seeds; वपन्ति = (they) sow; गायन्तः = singing; नवजीवनम् = new life.

Translation: The rainy season has arrived. Everywhere in the sky dark clouds thunder; lightning flashes moment by moment; a cool wind blows; heavy rain falls. With the rain-water the earth has turned green. In the forests the peacocks, uttering their cry, dance with joy. The chataka birds gaze at the sky to drink the raindrops. The rivers, becoming full of water, flow swiftly; ponds and wells fill with water. The farmers, delighted, plough their fields and sow seeds; they work singing. Children play in the rain. All nature receives new life. That is why the poets call the rainy season 'the giver of life'.

पद्यानि — Four famous public-domain verses on वर्षा

1) ऋतुसंहारम् 2.1 (कालिदासः) — the monsoon arrives like a king:
ससीकराम्भोधरमत्तकुञ्जरस्तडित्पताकोऽशनिशब्दमर्दलः।
समागतो राजवदुद्धतद्युतिर्घनागमः कामिजनप्रियः प्रिये॥
शब्दार्थ: प्रिये = O beloved!; ससीकर = accompanied by spray (शीकरः = fine water-drops); अम्भोधर = cloud (water-bearer); मत्तकुञ्जरः = rutting elephant; तडित् = lightning; पताका = banner, flag; अशनि = thunderbolt; शब्दः = sound; मर्दलः = a drum; समागतः = has arrived; राजवत् = like a king; उद्धतद्युतिः = of proud, lofty splendour; घनागमः = the arrival of the clouds, i.e. the monsoon; कामिजनप्रियः = dear to lovers.
अन्वयः: प्रिये! ससीकर-अम्भोधर-मत्तकुञ्जरः तडित्पताकः अशनिशब्दमर्दलः उद्धतद्युतिः कामिजनप्रियः घनागमः राजवत् समागतः।
Translation: O beloved! The monsoon has arrived like a king in proud splendour — the spray-laden clouds are his rutting elephants, the lightning his banner, the crash of thunder his drum; and he is dear to lovers.
Appreciation: This is a sustained उपमा — every element of a royal procession (elephants, banner, drum) is matched to an element of the monsoon (clouds, lightning, thunder). The compounds themselves (तडित्पताकः, अशनिशब्दमर्दलः — both बहुव्रीहि describing घनागमः) carry the picture.

2) मेघदूतम् 1 (कालिदासः) — the exiled yaksha:
कश्चित्कान्ताविरहगुरुणा स्वाधिकारात्प्रमत्तः शापेनास्तंगमितमहिमा वर्षभोग्येण भर्तुः।
यक्षश्चक्रे जनकतनयास्नानपुण्योदकेषु स्निग्धच्छायातरुषु वसतिं रामगिर्याश्रमेषु॥
शब्दार्थ: कश्चित् यक्षः = a certain yaksha; स्वाधिकारात् प्रमत्तः = negligent in his own duty; भर्तुः = of his master (कुबेर); शापेन = by the curse; वर्षभोग्येण = to be endured for one year; अस्तंगमितमहिमा = whose glory had set (been eclipsed); कान्ताविरहगुरुणा = made heavy by separation (विरह) from his beloved (कान्ता); जनकतनया = the daughter of Janaka, i.e. Sita; स्नानपुण्योदकेषु = whose waters were made holy by (Sita's) bathing; स्निग्धच्छायातरुषु = having trees of dense (soothing) shade; रामगिरि-आश्रमेषु = in the hermitages of Mount Ramagiri; वसतिं चक्रे = made (his) dwelling.
अन्वयः: स्वाधिकारात् प्रमत्तः कश्चित् यक्षः, कान्ताविरहगुरुणा वर्षभोग्येण भर्तुः शापेन अस्तंगमितमहिमा, जनकतनयास्नानपुण्योदकेषु स्निग्धच्छायातरुषु रामगिर्याश्रमेषु वसतिं चक्रे।
Translation: A certain yaksha, negligent in his duty, his glory eclipsed by his master's curse — a curse heavy because it separated him from his beloved and had to be endured for a full year — made his dwelling among the hermitages of Ramagiri, whose waters were hallowed by Sita's bathing and whose trees gave dense shade.

3) मेघदूतम् 2 (कालिदासः) — the cloud on the first day of Ashadha:
तस्मिन्नद्रौ कतिचिदबलाविप्रयुक्तः स कामी नीत्वा मासान्कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः।
आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे मेघमाश्लिष्टसानुं वप्रक्रीडापरिणतगजप्रेक्षणीयं ददर्श॥
शब्दार्थ: तस्मिन् अद्रौ = on that mountain; कतिचित् मासान् नीत्वा = having passed some months; अबलाविप्रयुक्तः = separated from his wife; सः कामी = that love-lorn one; कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः = his forearm (प्रकोष्ठः) left bare by the slipping (भ्रंश) of his golden bracelet (कनकवलय) — he had grown thin with grief; आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे = on the first day of (the month) Ashadha; आश्लिष्टसानुम् मेघम् = a cloud embracing the mountain-ridge (सानुः = peak, ridge); वप्रक्रीडापरिणतगजप्रेक्षणीयम् = lovely to behold like an elephant bent down in butting-play (वप्रक्रीडा) against a bank; ददर्श = (he) saw.
अन्वयः: अबलाविप्रयुक्तः सः कामी तस्मिन् अद्रौ कतिचित् मासान् नीत्वा, कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः, आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे आश्लिष्टसानुं वप्रक्रीडापरिणतगजप्रेक्षणीयं मेघं ददर्श।
Translation: Separated from his wife, that love-lorn yaksha passed some months on that mountain, his forearm bare where the golden bracelet had slipped from his wasted wrist; then, on the first day of Ashadha, he saw a cloud embracing the mountain-ridge, beautiful as an elephant stooped in butting-play against a bank.
Appreciation: The sight of the first monsoon cloud — which makes even happy minds wistful — overwhelms the separated lover, and he resolves to make the cloud his messenger; thus the whole मेघदूत is born from this वर्षा-moment. The dominant sentiment is विप्रलम्भशृङ्गारः (love-in-separation).

4) चातकान्योक्तिः (traditionally ascribed to भर्तृहरिः, नीतिशतकम्) — some clouds rain, some only thunder:
रे रे चातक सावधानमनसा मित्र क्षणं श्रूयतां
अम्भोदा बहवो हि सन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैतादृशाः।
केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति वसुधां गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा
यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः॥
शब्दार्थ: रे रे चातक = O chataka!; सावधानमनसा = with an attentive mind; मित्र = friend; क्षणं श्रूयताम् = let it be heard for a moment; अम्भोदाः = clouds (water-givers); बहवः = many; गगने = in the sky; सर्वे अपि = all of them; न एतादृशाः = not of the same kind; केचित् = some; वृष्टिभिः = with showers; आर्द्रयन्ति = moisten, wet; वसुधाम् = the earth; गर्जन्ति = thunder; वृथा = in vain; यं यं पश्यसि = whomsoever you see; तस्य तस्य पुरतः = before each of them; मा ब्रूहि = do not utter; दीनं वचः = piteous words.
अन्वयः: रे रे चातक मित्र! सावधानमनसा क्षणं श्रूयताम्। गगने अम्भोदाः बहवः हि सन्ति, (परं) सर्वे अपि न एतादृशाः। केचित् वृष्टिभिः वसुधाम् आर्द्रयन्ति, केचित् (तु) वृथा गर्जन्ति। (अतः) यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतः दीनं वचः मा ब्रूहि।
Translation: O chataka, my friend, listen attentively for a moment. There are many clouds in the sky, but not all are alike: some moisten the earth with their showers, while others merely thunder in vain. So do not utter your piteous plea before every one you see.
Appreciation: This is an अन्योक्तिः (allegorical address): through the chataka — who by poetic convention (कविसमय) drinks only raindrops — the poet really addresses human beings: do not beg from everyone; the truly generous give like raining clouds, while the boastful only thunder. Preserve your self-respect and appeal only to the worthy.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar drawn from the texts

(A) सन्धिः. Examples with सन्धि-विच्छेद (splitting):
  • घन + आगमः → घनागमः (अ + आ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः) — 'the coming of the clouds'.
  • सम् + आगतः → समागतः; शापेन + अस्तंगमितमहिमा → शापेनास्तंगमितमहिमा (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः).
  • न + एतादृशाः → नैतादृशाः (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धिसन्धिः).
  • सर्वे + अपि → सर्वेऽपि (ए + अ; the अ is elided and marked by the avagraha ऽ — पूर्वरूपसन्धिः).
  • तस्मिन् + अद्रौ → तस्मिन्नद्रौ (the न् is doubled before a vowel after a short vowel — ङमुडागमसन्धिः).
  • मेघम् + आश्लिष्टसानुम् → मेघमाश्लिष्टसानुम् (म् joins the following vowel).

(B) समासः. वर्णन-poetry packs whole pictures into compounds:
  • कर्मधारयः (descriptive): नीलमेघः = नीलः चासौ मेघः ('the blue-dark cloud').
  • षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः: घनागमः = घनानाम् आगमः ('arrival OF the clouds'); जनकतनया = जनकस्य तनया ('Janaka's daughter', Sita); कामिजनप्रियः = कामिजनानां प्रियः ('dear TO lovers').
  • बहुव्रीहिः (possessive, describing something else): तडित्पताकः = तडित् पताका यस्य सः ('he whose banner is the lightning' — the monsoon-king); अशनिशब्दमर्दलः = अशनेः शब्दः एव मर्दलः यस्य सः ('whose drum is the thunder-crash'); आश्लिष्टसानुः (मेघः) = आश्लिष्टः सानुः येन सः ('by whom the ridge is embraced').

(C) विभक्तिः. Case forms in the texts: गगने, वृष्टौ, प्रथमदिवसे, क्षेत्रेषु = सप्तमी (in/on); वृष्टिभिः, हलैः, वेगेन, शापेन = तृतीया (by/with); आषाढस्य, भर्तुः, तस्य = षष्ठी (of); वसुधाम्, मेघम्, वसतिम् = द्वितीया (object); मासान् = द्वितीया बहुवचन (duration of time — कालात्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया).

(D) कृदन्ताः. Verbal derivatives: क्त-प्रत्ययः (past participle): समागतः, आश्लिष्टः, प्रमत्तः; क्त्वा-प्रत्ययः (having done): कृत्वा, नीत्वा, भूत्वा, कृषित्वा; शतृ-प्रत्ययः (present participle): गायन्तः, गर्जन्; तुमुन्-प्रत्ययः (in order to): पातुम्; अनीयर्-प्रत्ययः (worthy of): प्रेक्षणीयम् ('worth beholding'). Note also ददर्श = लिट् लकारः (the perfect tense) of दृश् — 'he saw (long ago)', the classic narrative past of kavya.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you studied the great tradition of ऋतुवर्णन (season-description) in Sanskrit kavya and its crown, the description of वर्षा. You read an original prose passage picturing the monsoon — thundering clouds, lightning, dancing peacocks, brimming rivers, sowing farmers — with full शब्दार्थ. You then studied four public-domain verses: ऋतुसंहार 2.1, where the monsoon arrives like a king with cloud-elephants, lightning-banner and thunder-drum; मेघदूत 1-2, where the exiled yaksha, wasted by separation, sees on the first day of आषाढ a cloud embracing the ridge like a playing elephant; and the चातक-अन्योक्ति, teaching through the rain-bird that some clouds rain while others only thunder — appeal only to the generous. From these you drew grammar: दीर्घ, वृद्धि, पूर्वरूप and other सन्धि with विच्छेद; the descriptive compounds (कर्मधारय, तत्पुरुष, बहुव्रीहि) that carry kavya's pictures; the common विभक्ति roles; and the कृदन्त suffixes क्त, क्त्वा, शतृ, तुमुन् and अनीयर्, plus the perfect ददर्श. Memorise at least two of the verses — they are among the most beautiful monsoon lines ever composed.

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Vocabulary of the Rainy Season

chapter_summary.title: वर्षर्तुवर्णनम् (Varsharttu-Varnanam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary for Chapter 13. It presents the kavya tradition of describing the rainy season, an original prose picture of the monsoon, four public-domain वर्षा verses from Kalidasa and the chataka allegory, and the grammar — sandhi, samasa, vibhakti, krdanta — drawn from them.

sections.heading: The kavya tradition of season-description
bullets: Classical Sanskrit poetry treats प्रकृतिवर्णन — and especially the six seasons (वसन्त, ग्रीष्म, वर्षा, शरद्, हेमन्त, शिशिर) — as a defining ornament of kavya.
Kalidasa's ऋतुसंहारम् devotes one canto to each season; the second canto describes वर्षा, and his मेघदूतम् is built entirely on a monsoon cloud.
मेघदूतम् is a खण्डकाव्य (lyric/messenger poem) composed throughout in the मन्दाक्रान्ता metre; its dominant sentiment is विप्रलम्भशृङ्गार (love-in-separation).
वर्षा is traditionally the months श्रावण and भाद्रपद, heralded by the first cloud of आषाढ.

sections.heading: The monsoon in prose — a living picture
bullets: Dark clouds thunder in the sky (नीलाः मेघाः गर्जन्ति), lightning flashes (तडित् चमकति), and heavy rain turns the earth green (वसुधा हरिता जाता).
Peacocks cry (केकारवम्) and dance; the chataka waits for raindrops; rivers run full and swift; ponds and wells fill.
Farmers plough with हल and sow seeds singing — the rains are the life of agriculture, so poets call वर्षा 'जीवनदाता' (giver of life).
The passage supplies core vocabulary: वृष्टिः, गगनम्, वेगेन, जलपूर्णाः, बीजानि, कृषित्वा, गायन्तः.

sections.heading: The monsoon-king and the yaksha's cloud
bullets: ऋतुसंहार 2.1: the monsoon (घनागमः) arrives राजवत् — spray-laden clouds are its rutting elephants, lightning its banner (तडित्पताकः), thunder its drum (अशनिशब्दमर्दलः); it is कामिजनप्रियः, dear to lovers.
मेघदूत 1: a yaksha, negligent in duty, is cursed by his master (Kubera) to a year's exile; his glory eclipsed, he dwells at रामगिरि, whose waters Sita's bathing made holy.
मेघदूत 2: wasted by separation — his golden bracelet slips from his bare forearm — he sees on आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे a cloud embracing the ridge, lovely as an elephant bent in butting-play.
That sight births the whole poem: the yaksha makes the cloud his messenger to his beloved in Alaka.

sections.heading: The chataka allegory — rain, not thunder
bullets: The चातक, by poetic convention, drinks only raindrops — so it must beg the clouds for water.
The poet warns: many clouds fill the sky, but not all are alike — some moisten the earth with showers (केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति वसुधाम्), some only thunder in vain (गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा).
As an अन्योक्ति the verse really addresses people: do not utter piteous pleas before everyone; appeal only to the truly generous, and keep your self-respect.
Generous helpers act quietly like raining clouds; boastful ones merely thunder.

sections.heading: Grammar from the texts
bullets: सन्धिः: घन + आगमः = घनागमः (दीर्घ); न + एतादृशाः = नैतादृशाः (वृद्धि); सर्वे + अपि = सर्वेऽपि (पूर्वरूप, avagraha); तस्मिन् + अद्रौ = तस्मिन्नद्रौ (ङमुडागम — doubling of न्).
समासः: नीलमेघः (कर्मधारय); घनागमः, जनकतनया, कामिजनप्रियः (षष्ठीतत्पुरुष); तडित्पताकः, अशनिशब्दमर्दलः, आश्लिष्टसानुः (बहुव्रीहि describing another noun).
विभक्तिः: गगने/प्रथमदिवसे (सप्तमी), वृष्टिभिः/हलैः/शापेन (तृतीया), आषाढस्य/भर्तुः (षष्ठी), वसुधाम्/मेघम् (द्वितीया), मासान् (द्वितीया of duration).
कृदन्ताः: समागतः/आश्लिष्टः (क्त), नीत्वा/कृत्वा/भूत्वा (क्त्वा), गायन्तः/गर्जन् (शतृ), पातुम् (तुमुन्), प्रेक्षणीयम् (अनीयर्); ददर्श is लिट् (perfect) of दृश्.

key_takeaways: ऋतुवर्णन — the description of the six seasons — is a defining ornament of Sanskrit kavya, and वर्षा is its favourite season.
Kalidasa's ऋतुसंहार (canto 2) and मेघदूत — a खण्डकाव्य in मन्दाक्रान्ता metre — are the classic models of monsoon poetry.
In ऋतुसंहार 2.1 the monsoon arrives like a king: clouds for elephants, lightning for banner, thunder for drum — a sustained उपमा.
In मेघदूत the exiled, love-lorn yaksha sees the first cloud of आषाढ embracing the ridge like a playing elephant — and makes it his messenger.
The चातक-अन्योक्ति teaches: some clouds rain, some only thunder — appeal only to the truly generous, and never beg from everyone.
वर्णन-poetry packs its pictures into compounds: कर्मधारय, षष्ठीतत्पुरुष and above all बहुव्रीहि (तडित्पताकः = 'whose banner is the lightning').
Key grammar: दीर्घ/वृद्धि/पूर्वरूप/ङमुडागम सन्धि; विभक्ति roles; कृदन्त suffixes क्त, क्त्वा, शतृ, तुमुन्, अनीयर्; and the perfect ददर्श (लिट्).

glossary.definition: The poetic description of the seasons; a standard and beloved subject of classical Sanskrit kavya.
The rainy season (monsoon), traditionally the months श्रावण and भाद्रपद; called 'जीवनदाता' because it gives new life to earth and agriculture.
The 'arrival of the clouds', i.e. the onset of the monsoon; a षष्ठीतत्पुरुष compound (घनानाम् आगमः).
A cloud — literally 'water-giver' / 'water-bearer'; synonyms of मेघः used in the verses.
Lightning (also विद्युत्); in ऋतुसंहार 2.1 it is the monsoon-king's banner (तडित्पताकः).
The thunderbolt; अशनिशब्दः, the crash of thunder, serves as the monsoon-king's drum (मर्दलः).
A bird which, by poetic convention (कविसमय), drinks only falling raindrops — hence the emblem of the hopeful supplicant.
The peacock, which utters its cry (केकारवः) and dances with joy at the coming of the rains.
The semi-divine attendant of Kubera whose year-long exile at Ramagiri, away from his beloved, frames the मेघदूत.
An allegorical address: the poet speaks to a bird, tree or cloud but really means human beings — as in the chataka verse.
The simile; e.g. the monsoon arriving राजवत् ('like a king') and the cloud looking like an elephant at butting-play.
The slow, stately metre of 17 syllables per quarter in which the entire मेघदूत is composed.
The sentiment of love-in-separation, dominant in the मेघदूत — longing intensified by the monsoon.
The possessive compound describing another noun, e.g. तडित्पताकः = 'he whose banner is the lightning'.
A verbal derivative formed with a कृत् suffix — क्त (समागतः), क्त्वा (नीत्वा), शतृ (गायन्तः), तुमुन् (पातुम्), अनीयर् (प्रेक्षणीयम्).

worksheet.title: Worksheet — वर्षर्तुवर्णनम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 13)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit in Devanagari and give explanations in English. Refer to the prose passage and the four verses of the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate into simple English:
ससीकराम्भोधरमत्तकुञ्जरस्तडित्पताकोऽशनिशब्दमर्दलः।
समागतो राजवदुद्धतद्युतिर्घनागमः कामिजनप्रियः प्रिये॥
questions.answer: O beloved! The monsoon (घनागमः) has arrived like a king in proud splendour — the spray-laden clouds are his rutting elephants, the lightning his banner, the crash of thunder his drum; and he is dear to lovers (कामिजनप्रियः).
questions.explanation: Ritusamhara 2.1 — a sustained simile matching the monsoon to a royal procession.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: अम्भोदः, तडित्, वसुधा, कुञ्जरः, सानुः.
questions.answer: अम्भोदः = cloud ('water-giver'); तडित् = lightning; वसुधा = the earth; कुञ्जरः = elephant; सानुः = mountain-peak/ridge.
questions.explanation: Core rainy-season vocabulary from the verses.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) घनागमः (b) नैतादृशाः, and name each sandhi.
questions.answer: (a) घनागमः = घन + आगमः (अ + आ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः). (b) नैतादृशाः = न + एतादृशाः (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धिसन्धिः).
questions.explanation: Both occur in the chapter's verses; splitting joined forms is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: Give the विग्रह (dissolution) and name the समास of: (a) घनागमः (b) तडित्पताकः.
questions.answer: (a) घनागमः = घनानाम् आगमः — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः ('arrival of the clouds'). (b) तडित्पताकः = तडित् पताका यस्य सः — बहुव्रीहिः ('he whose banner is the lightning', describing घनागमः).
questions.explanation: Descriptive compounds carry the picture in varnana poetry.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति and its role: गगने, वृष्टिभिः, आषाढस्य, वसुधाम्.
questions.answer: गगने = सप्तमी (locative) 'in the sky'; वृष्टिभिः = तृतीया बहुवचन (instrumental) 'with showers'; आषाढस्य = षष्ठी (genitive) 'of Ashadha'; वसुधाम् = द्वितीया (accusative) 'the earth' (object).
questions.explanation: All four forms occur in the chapter's verses.

questions.question: 'मेघदूतम्' इति काव्ये दूतः कः? (Who is the messenger in the Meghaduta?)
questions.explanation: The yaksha makes a monsoon cloud his messenger to his beloved — hence the title 'Cloud Messenger'.

questions.question: ऋतुसंहारे वर्षावर्णनं द्वितीये सर्गे अस्ति। (In the Ritusamhara, the description of the rains is in the second canto.)
questions.explanation: The Ritusamhara begins with summer (ग्रीष्म); its second canto describes वर्षा.

questions.question: Explain the चातक-अन्योक्ति 'रे रे चातक...' — give its meaning, explain the अन्योक्ति device, and state its lesson for today.
questions.answer:
Meaning: The poet tells his friend the chataka to listen attentively: there are many clouds in the sky, but not all are alike — some moisten the earth with showers, while others merely thunder in vain; so the bird should not utter its piteous plea before every cloud it sees.
Device: This is an अन्योक्तिः (allegorical address) — the poet speaks to the bird, but really addresses human beings. The chataka, who by poetic convention drinks only raindrops, stands for the needy person; raining clouds stand for the truly generous; thundering clouds for boastful people who promise but never give.
Lesson: Do not beg from everyone; judge people by their deeds, not their noise; approach only the genuinely generous, and preserve your self-respect. Today too, loud promises (mere 'thunder') must be distinguished from quiet help (actual 'rain').
questions.explanation: Full marks require the literal meaning, the identification and working of the अन्योक्ति, and a modern application.

questions.question: Compose four simple Sanskrit sentences in Devanagari describing the rainy season (वर्षा), and give their English meanings.
questions.answer:
1. गगने मेघाः गर्जन्ति। (Clouds thunder in the sky.)
2. मयूराः आनन्देन नृत्यन्ति। (Peacocks dance with joy.)
3. नद्यः जलपूर्णाः वेगेन वहन्ति। (The rivers, full of water, flow swiftly.)
4. कृषकाः क्षेत्रेषु बीजानि वपन्ति। (Farmers sow seeds in the fields.)
Together these picture the monsoon: thundering clouds, dancing peacocks, brimming rivers and sowing farmers.
questions.explanation: Simple subject-verb sentences using the chapter's vocabulary; any four correct sentences on the theme earn full marks.

questions.question: Why was the yaksha living at Ramagiri, and in what condition did he see the cloud on the first day of Ashadha? (Answer from मेघदूत 1-2.)
questions.answer: The yaksha had been negligent in his duty, so his master (Kubera) cursed him to a year's exile (वर्षभोग्येण शापेन), stripping his glory; separated from his beloved, he dwelt in the hermitages of Ramagiri. Months of grief had wasted him — his golden bracelet slipped from his bare forearm (कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः). In that state, on आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे, he saw a cloud embracing the mountain-ridge, lovely as an elephant bent in butting-play against a bank.
questions.explanation: Combines the narrative facts of Meghaduta verses 1 and 2.

questions.question: कालिदासस्य ऋतुवर्णनप्रधानं काव्यं किम्? (Which work of Kalidasa is devoted entirely to the seasons?)
questions.explanation: The Ritusamhara ('Garland of the Seasons') devotes one canto to each of the six seasons.

questions.question: 'मेघदूतम्' इति काव्ये दूतः कः अस्ति?
questions.explanation: The exiled yaksha makes a monsoon cloud (मेघः) his messenger — hence 'The Cloud Messenger'.

questions.question: भारतीयपरम्परायां ऋतवः कति सन्ति?
questions.explanation: Six seasons: वसन्त, ग्रीष्म, वर्षा, शरद्, हेमन्त, शिशिर.

questions.question: ऋतुसंहारे वर्षावर्णनं कस्मिन् सर्गे अस्ति?
questions.explanation: The Ritusamhara opens with summer (ग्रीष्म); the second canto describes the rains.

questions.question: मेघदूते यक्षः कस्य शापेन रामगिरौ न्यवसत्?
questions.explanation: 'भर्तुः शापेन' — by the curse of his master, Kubera, lord of the yakshas.

questions.question: मेघदूतं कस्मिन् काव्यप्रकारे गण्यते?
questions.explanation: The Meghaduta is a short lyric (खण्डकाव्य), not an epic महाकाव्य.

questions.question: 'ऋतुवर्णनम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: ऋतु = season, वर्णनम् = description — a favourite subject of Sanskrit kavya.

questions.question: यक्षः वसतिं कुत्र चक्रे?
questions.explanation: He dwelt in the hermitages of Ramagiri, whose waters Sita's bathing had made holy.

questions.question: परम्परानुसारं वर्षर्तोः मासौ कौ?
questions.explanation: In the traditional reckoning वर्षा comprises the months श्रावण and भाद्रपद.

questions.question: पाठानुसारं कवयः वर्षर्तुं किम् इति वदन्ति?
questions.explanation: Because the rains give new life to the earth and to agriculture, poets call वर्षा the 'giver of life'.

questions.question: 'समागतो राजवत्...' इति पद्ये घनागमः केन सह तुल्यते?
questions.explanation: राजवत् समागतः — the monsoon arrives 'like a king' with elephants, banner and drum.

questions.question: ऋतुसंहारपद्ये तडित् (विद्युत्) राज्ञः किं कल्पिता?
questions.explanation: तडित्पताकः — the lightning is the monsoon-king's banner.

questions.question: तस्मिन् एव पद्ये अशनिशब्दः (thunder) किं कल्पितः?
questions.explanation: अशनिशब्दमर्दलः — the crash of thunder is the king's drum (मर्दल).

questions.question: आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे यक्षः किं ददर्श?
questions.explanation: On the first day of Ashadha the yaksha saw a cloud embracing the mountain-ridge.

questions.question: 'रे रे चातक...' इति पद्ये कविः कं सम्बोधयति?
questions.explanation: The poet addresses his 'friend' the chataka bird — though the real target is humankind.

questions.question: यक्षस्य शापः कियत्कालं भोग्यः आसीत्?
questions.explanation: 'वर्षभोग्येण' — the curse was to be endured for one full year.

questions.question: मेघदूतस्य प्रथमं पदं किम्?
questions.explanation: The poem opens 'कश्चित्कान्ताविरहगुरुणा...' — 'a certain (yaksha)...'.

questions.question: यक्षस्य प्रकोष्ठः कस्मात् रिक्तः अभवत्?
questions.explanation: Wasted by grief, his wrist grew thin and the golden bracelet slipped off — कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः.

questions.question: 'यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः' — अत्र कविः चातकं किं कर्तुं निषेधति?
questions.explanation: The bird is told NOT to utter piteous words before every cloud it sees.

questions.question: 'मेघः' इत्यस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायाम् अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: मेघः = cloud; synonyms in the chapter include अम्भोदः, अम्भोधरः and घनः.

questions.question: ऋतुसंहारपद्ये मेघाः राज्ञः के कल्पिताः? (In Ritusamhara 2.1, the clouds are imagined as the king's what?)
questions.explanation: ससीकराम्भोधरमत्तकुञ्जरः — the spray-laden clouds are the monsoon-king's rutting elephants.

questions.question: घनागमः 'कामिजनप्रियः' इति किमर्थम् उच्यते?
options: Because lovers delight in the romantic monsoon atmosphere
Because kings love to fight in the rains
Because birds fly away in the monsoon
questions.answer: Because lovers delight in the romantic monsoon atmosphere
questions.explanation: The cool, cloud-darkened monsoon is by convention the season of love — hence 'dear to lovers'.

questions.question: 'वप्रक्रीडापरिणतगजप्रेक्षणीयम्' — the cloud looked beautiful like what?
options: An elephant bent down in butting-play against a bank
A lion leaping upon its prey
A swan gliding on a lake
questions.answer: An elephant bent down in butting-play against a bank
questions.explanation: वप्रक्रीडा is an elephant's sport of butting a mound; the ridge-hugging cloud resembled such a stooping elephant.

questions.question: कविसमयानुसारं चातकः किं पिबति?
questions.explanation: By poetic convention (कविसमय) the chataka drinks only falling raindrops.

questions.question: 'गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा' इत्यनेन के मेघाः सूचिताः?
questions.explanation: Some clouds merely thunder in vain and give no rain — like people who boast but never help.

questions.question: वर्षासु मयूराः किं कुर्वन्ति?
questions.explanation: Peacocks utter their केकारव and dance with joy at the coming of the clouds.

questions.question: पाठानुसारं वर्षासु कृषकाः किं कुर्वन्ति?
questions.explanation: The delighted farmers plough with हल and sow seeds, singing as they work.

questions.question: 'आश्लिष्टसानुं मेघम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
options: A cloud hidden behind the mountain
A cloud driven away by the wind
questions.explanation: आश्लिष्टः सानुः येन — the cloud clung to (embraced) the ridge of Ramagiri.

questions.question: वर्षासु नद्यः कीदृश्यः भवन्ति?
questions.explanation: नद्यः जलपूर्णाः भूत्वा वेगेन वहन्ति — the rivers become full and flow swiftly.

questions.question: मेघदूते 'अबलाविप्रयुक्तः' इति पदेन यक्षस्य का अवस्था सूचिता?
questions.explanation: अबला = wife/beloved, विप्रयुक्तः = separated — the yaksha was parted from his wife.

questions.question: 'अम्भोदः' इत्यस्य पर्यायपदं किम्?
questions.explanation: अम्भः (water) + द (giver) = cloud; a synonym of मेघः.

questions.question: 'वसुधा' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: वसुधा = the earth ('bearer of wealth'); the clouds moisten the वसुधा with showers.

questions.question: 'तडित्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: तडित् = lightning (विद्युत्); in the verse it is the monsoon-king's banner.

questions.question: 'कुञ्जरः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: कुञ्जरः = elephant; the clouds are मत्तकुञ्जराः, rutting elephants.

questions.question: 'अशनिः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: अशनिः = the thunderbolt; अशनिशब्दः is the crash of thunder, the king's drum.

questions.question: 'शीकरः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: शीकरः = fine drops of water, drizzle-spray; the clouds are ससीकर, spray-laden.

questions.question: 'मर्दलः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: मर्दलः is a drum; the thunder serves as the monsoon-king's drum.

questions.question: 'केकारवः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: केका is the peacock's cry; केकारवः = the sound of the peacock.

questions.question: 'अद्रिः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: अद्रिः = mountain; तस्मिन् अद्रौ = 'on that mountain' (Ramagiri).

questions.question: 'सस्यम्' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: सस्यम् = standing crop/grain, which the monsoon rains nourish.

questions.question: मेघदूते 'प्रकोष्ठः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: प्रकोष्ठः = the forearm; the yaksha's forearm was left bare when his bracelet slipped.

questions.question: 'सानुः' इत्यस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.explanation: सानुः = the ridge or table-land of a mountain; the cloud embraced the सानु.

questions.question: 'रे रे चातक...' इति पद्ये कः अलङ्कारः प्रधानः?
questions.explanation: The poet addresses the chataka but really means human beings — the device of अन्योक्ति (allegorical address).

questions.question: 'राजवत् समागतः' इत्यत्र कः अलङ्कारः?
questions.explanation: The monsoon is explicitly compared to a king with the comparative suffix वत् ('like') — a simile (उपमा).

questions.question: मेघदूतस्य छन्दः किम्?
questions.explanation: The entire Meghaduta is composed in the slow, stately मन्दाक्रान्ता metre (17 syllables per quarter).

questions.question: मेघदूते प्रधानः रसः कः?
questions.explanation: The dominant sentiment is love-in-separation — the exiled yaksha longing for his distant beloved.

questions.question: चातकपद्यस्य नीतिः (moral) का?
options: Seek help only from the truly generous
Never drink water in the rains
One should thunder loudly like a cloud
questions.answer: Seek help only from the truly generous
questions.explanation: Since some clouds rain and some only thunder, the needy should appeal only to the worthy and keep their self-respect.

questions.question: 'गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा' — मनुष्यलोके एतादृशाः के?
options: ये बहु वदन्ति परं किमपि न कुर्वन्ति
questions.answer: ये बहु वदन्ति परं किमपि न कुर्वन्ति
questions.explanation: The vainly-thundering clouds stand for people who promise loudly but never actually help.

questions.question: 'मेघः गजः इव प्रेक्षणीयः' — अत्र उपमानं किम्?
questions.explanation: The thing compared TO is the उपमान (the elephant); the cloud (मेघः) is the उपमेय.

questions.question: अन्योक्तौ कविः वस्तुतः कान् लक्ष्यीकरोति?
questions.explanation: In an अन्योक्ति the ostensible addressee is a bird or object, but the real target is human conduct.

questions.question: घनागमस्य 'उद्धतद्युतिः' इति विशेषणं किं सूचयति?
options: Proud, lofty splendour like a king's
questions.answer: Proud, lofty splendour like a king's
questions.explanation: उद्धत (lofty, proud) + द्युति (splendour) — the monsoon enters with royal brilliance.

questions.question: 'घनागमः' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: अ + आ = आ (दीर्घसन्धिः): घन + आगमः = घनागमः.

questions.question: 'नैतादृशाः' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: अ + ए = ऐ (वृद्धिसन्धिः): न + एतादृशाः = नैतादृशाः, 'not of such a kind'.

questions.question: 'तस्मिन्नद्रौ' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: After a short vowel, final न् doubles before a vowel (ङमुडागम): तस्मिन् + अद्रौ = तस्मिन्नद्रौ.

questions.question: 'सर्वेऽपि' इत्यत्र कः सन्धिः?
questions.explanation: सर्वे + अपि: after ए the following अ is elided and marked with the avagraha (ऽ) — पूर्वरूपसन्धिः.

questions.question: 'समागतः' इत्यस्य सन्धिविच्छेदः कः?
questions.explanation: सम् + आगतः = समागतः, 'arrived, come together'.

questions.question: 'घनागमः' (घनानाम् आगमः) इति कः समासः?
questions.explanation: The first member stands in the genitive relation — 'arrival OF the clouds' — hence षष्ठीतत्पुरुष.

questions.question: 'तडित्पताकः' (तडित् पताका यस्य सः) इति कः समासः?
questions.explanation: The compound describes ANOTHER (the monsoon-king) — 'he WHOSE banner is the lightning' — hence बहुव्रीहि.

questions.question: 'नीलमेघः' (नीलः चासौ मेघः) इति कः समासः?
questions.explanation: Adjective + noun in the same case ('the dark-blue cloud') — a descriptive कर्मधारय.

questions.question: 'जनकतनया' इत्यस्य विग्रहः कः?
questions.explanation: 'The daughter OF Janaka' (Sita) — genitive dissolution, षष्ठीतत्पुरुष.

questions.question: 'कामिजनप्रियः' इत्यस्य विग्रहः कः?
questions.explanation: 'Dear TO (of) lovers' — genitive dissolution; the monsoon is beloved of all lovers.

questions.question: शापेन + अस्तंगमितमहिमा = शापेनास्तंगमितमहिमा — अत्र कः सन्धिः?
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ — the two short vowels merge into one long आ (दीर्घसन्धिः).

questions.question: 'गगने' इत्यत्र का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: गगने = 'IN the sky' — locative (सप्तमी) singular.

questions.question: 'वृष्टिभिः' इत्यत्र का विभक्तिः किं वचनं च?
questions.explanation: वृष्टिभिः = 'WITH showers' — instrumental (तृतीया) plural of वृष्टि.

questions.question: 'आषाढस्य' इत्यत्र का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: आषाढस्य = 'OF Ashadha' — genitive (षष्ठी) singular.

questions.question: 'वसुधाम्' इत्यत्र का विभक्तिः?
questions.explanation: वसुधाम् is the object of आर्द्रयन्ति ('they moisten THE EARTH') — accusative (द्वितीया).

questions.question: 'नीत्वा' इत्यत्र कः प्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: नी + क्त्वा = नीत्वा, 'having passed/led' — the absolutive suffix.

questions.question: 'समागतः' इत्यत्र कः प्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: सम् + आ + गम् + क्त = समागतः — past passive participle 'arrived'.

questions.question: 'गायन्तः' इत्यत्र कः प्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: गै + शतृ = गायत्, plural गायन्तः 'singing' — the present participle.

questions.question: 'प्रेक्षणीयम्' इत्यत्र कः प्रत्ययः?
questions.explanation: प्र + ईक्ष् + अनीयर् = प्रेक्षणीय, 'worth beholding' — a potential participle.

questions.question: 'ददर्श' इति रूपं कस्मिन् लकारे अस्ति?
questions.explanation: ददर्श is the reduplicated perfect (लिट्) of दृश् — the classic narrative past of kavya: 'he saw'.

questions.question: 'मेघाः गर्जन्ति' — English translation?
questions.explanation: मेघाः = clouds (subject, plural); गर्जन्ति = (they) thunder.

questions.question: 'Peacocks dance' — इत्यस्य शुद्धः संस्कृतानुवादः कः?
questions.explanation: Plural subject मयूराः takes the plural verb नृत्यन्ति.

questions.question: 'The farmer sows seeds' — इत्यस्य शुद्धः संस्कृतानुवादः कः?
questions.explanation: Singular subject कृषकः + neuter plural object बीजानि + singular verb वपति.

questions.question: 'नद्यः वेगेन वहन्ति' — English translation?
options: The clouds move with the wind
questions.explanation: नद्यः = rivers (plural); वेगेन = with speed (instrumental); वहन्ति = flow.

questions.question: ऋतुसंहारं कालिदासेन रचितम्। (The Ritusamhara was composed by Kalidasa.)
questions.explanation: The Ritusamhara, a lyric on the six seasons, is a work of Kalidasa.

questions.question: मेघदूते दूतः हंसः अस्ति। (In the Meghaduta the messenger is a swan.)
questions.explanation: The messenger is a monsoon cloud (मेघः), not a swan — hence the title 'Cloud Messenger'.

questions.question: ऋतुसंहारपद्ये घनागमः भिक्षुकः इव समागतः इति वर्णितम्। (In the Ritusamhara verse the monsoon is described as arriving like a beggar.)
questions.explanation: The monsoon arrives राजवत् — like a KING, with cloud-elephants, lightning-banner and thunder-drum.

questions.question: कविसमयानुसारं चातकः केवलं वृष्टिजलं पिबति। (By poetic convention the chataka drinks only rain-water.)
questions.explanation: The कविसमय (poetic convention) is that the chataka drinks only falling raindrops — hence its pleading to the clouds.

questions.question: 'घनागमः' इत्यत्र दीर्घसन्धिः अस्ति। (There is dirgha-sandhi in 'ghanagamah'.)
questions.explanation: घन + आगमः: अ + आ = आ, which is दीर्घसन्धिः.

questions.question: 'तडित्पताकः' इति कर्मधारयसमासः अस्ति। (The compound 'tadit-patakah' is a karmadharaya.)
questions.explanation: It is a बहुव्रीहि: तडित् पताका यस्य सः — 'he WHOSE banner is the lightning', describing the monsoon-king.

questions.question: 'गगने' इति पदे तृतीया विभक्तिः अस्ति। (The word 'gagane' is in the third (instrumental) case.)
questions.explanation: गगने is सप्तमी (locative) — 'IN the sky'.

questions.question: मेघदूतं मन्दाक्रान्ताछन्दसि रचितम्। (The Meghaduta is composed in the Mandakranta metre.)
questions.explanation: Every stanza of the Meghaduta is in मन्दाक्रान्ता — the slow, stately metre suited to longing.

questions.question: यक्षः आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे मेघं ददर्श। (The yaksha saw the cloud on the first day of Ashadha.)
questions.explanation: आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे — on the first day of the month Ashadha he saw the ridge-embracing cloud.

questions.question: वर्षासु नद्यः शुष्काः भवन्ति। (In the rainy season the rivers become dry.)
questions.explanation: The opposite: नद्यः जलपूर्णाः भूत्वा वेगेन वहन्ति — the rivers become full and flow swiftly.

questions.question: मेघदूतस्य रचयिता ________ अस्ति। (The author of the Meghaduta is ________.)
questions.explanation: Kalidasa composed the Meghaduta, the model of all messenger-poems.

questions.question: वर्षासु ________ केकारवं कृत्वा नृत्यन्ति। (In the rains the ________ cry and dance.)
questions.explanation: Peacocks (मयूराः) utter their केकारव and dance at the coming of the clouds.

questions.question: ________ केवलं वृष्टिजलं पिबति इति कविसमयः। (By poetic convention the ________ drinks only rain-water.)
questions.explanation: The chataka bird is the emblem of the hopeful supplicant who waits for raindrops.

questions.question: ऋतुसंहारपद्ये घनागमः ________ समागतः। (In the Ritusamhara verse the monsoon arrived ________ — 'like a king'.)
questions.explanation: राजवत् = 'like a king': समागतो राजवदुद्धतद्युतिः.

questions.question: यक्षः भर्तुः ________ अस्तंगमितमहिमा अभवत्। (The yaksha's glory was eclipsed by his master's ________.)
questions.explanation: शापेन = 'by the curse' (तृतीया) — Kubera's year-long curse of exile.

questions.question: 'अम्भोदः' इत्यस्य अर्थः ________ इति। (The meaning of 'ambhodah' is ________.)
questions.explanation: अम्भोदः ('water-giver') is a synonym of मेघः, cloud.

questions.question: 'वसुधा' इत्यस्य अर्थः ________ इति। (The meaning of 'vasudha' is ________.)
questions.explanation: वसुधा = the earth, 'bearer of wealth'.

questions.question: घन + आगमः = ________। (ghana + agamah = ________.)
questions.explanation: अ + आ = आ (दीर्घसन्धिः) gives घनागमः, 'the arrival of the clouds'.

questions.question: तस्मिन् + अद्रौ = ________। (tasmin + adrau = ________.)
questions.explanation: Final न् after a short vowel doubles before a vowel: तस्मिन्नद्रौ.

questions.question: 'नीत्वा' इति पदे ________ प्रत्ययः अस्ति। (The word 'nitva' contains the suffix ________.)
questions.explanation: नी + क्त्वा = नीत्वा, 'having passed' — the absolutive suffix.

questions.question: 'गगने' इति पदे ________ विभक्तिः अस्ति। (The word 'gagane' is in the ________ case.)
questions.explanation: गगने = 'in the sky' — locative (सप्तमी) singular.

questions.question: वर्षासु ________ जलपूर्णाः भूत्वा वेगेन वहन्ति। (In the rains the ________, becoming full, flow swiftly.)
questions.explanation: नद्यः (rivers) run full and swift in the monsoon.

questions.question: कृषकाः क्षेत्रेषु ________ वपन्ति। (The farmers sow ________ in the fields.)
questions.explanation: बीजानि (seeds, neuter plural) is the object of वपन्ति.

questions.question: यक्षः ________ मासस्य प्रथमदिवसे मेघं ददर्श। (The yaksha saw the cloud on the first day of the month ________.)
questions.explanation: आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे — the first day of Ashadha, the traditional onset of the monsoon.

questions.question: 'रे रे चातक' इति पद्यम् ________-अलङ्कारस्य प्रसिद्धम् उदाहरणम्। (The verse 're re chataka' is a famous example of the figure ________.)
questions.explanation: It is an अन्योक्ति: the bird is addressed, but human beings are meant.

questions.question: Briefly describe the tradition of ऋतुवर्णन in Sanskrit kavya, naming Kalidasa's two monsoon-related works.
questions.answer: Classical Sanskrit poets treated the description of nature — and above all of the six seasons (षड् ऋतवः) — as a defining ornament of kavya. Season-descriptions occur in almost every mahakavya, and Kalidasa raised them to an art: his ऋतुसंहारम् devotes one canto to each season (the second to वर्षा), and his मेघदूतम् is built entirely upon a single monsoon cloud seen on the first day of आषाढ, which the exiled yaksha makes his messenger.
questions.explanation: Expect: nature/season description as a kavya convention + ऋतुसंहार (canto 2 = varsha) + मेघदूत (monsoon cloud as messenger).

questions.question: षड् ऋतूनां नामानि संस्कृतेन लिखत। (Write the names of the six seasons in Sanskrit.)
questions.answer: वसन्तः (spring), ग्रीष्मः (summer), वर्षा (the rains), शरद् (autumn), हेमन्तः (early winter), शिशिरः (late winter).
questions.explanation: The six seasons of the traditional Indian year, two months each.

questions.question: In ऋतुसंहार 2.1 the monsoon arrives like a king. List the three elements of the royal procession and what each corresponds to in the monsoon.
questions.answer: (1) The king's rutting elephants (मत्तकुञ्जराः) = the spray-laden clouds (ससीकर-अम्भोधराः). (2) The king's banner (पताका) = the lightning (तडित्) — तडित्पताकः. (3) The king's drum (मर्दलः) = the crash of thunder (अशनिशब्दः) — अशनिशब्दमर्दलः.
questions.explanation: The sustained simile matches procession-elements to monsoon-elements one by one.

questions.question: Give in your own words the meaning of मेघदूत verse 1 (कश्चित्कान्ताविरहगुरुणा...).
questions.answer: A certain yaksha had been negligent in his duty, so his master (Kubera) cursed him: for one full year (वर्षभोग्येण) his glory would be eclipsed and he must live in exile. The curse was doubly heavy because it separated him from his beloved (कान्ताविरहगुरुणा). He made his dwelling among the hermitages of Mount Ramagiri, whose waters were hallowed by Sita's bathing and whose trees gave dense, soothing shade.
questions.explanation: Key points: negligence in duty, Kubera's one-year curse, separation from the beloved, dwelling at Ramagiri (Sita association, shady trees).

questions.question: किमर्थं यक्षः शप्तः? कः तं शशाप? (Why was the yaksha cursed, and who cursed him?)
questions.answer: यक्षः स्वाधिकारात् प्रमत्तः आसीत् — he was negligent in his appointed duty. His master (भर्तृ), Kubera, the lord of the yakshas, cursed him to lose his powers and live in exile for one year.
questions.explanation: स्वाधिकारात् प्रमत्तः + भर्तुः (कुबेरस्य) शापेन.

questions.question: Explain the compound 'कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः' — what does it literally say, and what does it tell us about the yaksha's state?
questions.answer: Literally: 'he whose forearm (प्रकोष्ठः) was left bare (रिक्त) by the slipping-off (भ्रंश) of his golden bracelet (कनकवलय)'. Months of grief in separation had made the yaksha so thin that his golden bracelet no longer stayed on his wrist. With one picture-packing compound Kalidasa conveys the lover wasting away in विरह without ever saying 'he grew thin'.
questions.explanation: Both the literal dissolution and the implied meaning (grief-caused emaciation, suggestion rather than statement) are required.

questions.question: What is the moral of the चातक verse 'रे रे चातक...'?
questions.answer: Not all clouds are alike: some moisten the earth with showers, others only thunder in vain. Likewise, not all people are generous — many merely boast. So one should not beg from everyone; appeal only to the truly generous, and preserve your self-respect.
questions.explanation: Judge by deeds, not noise; the raining cloud = the genuinely generous, the thundering cloud = the empty boaster.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: अम्भोदः, तडित्, कुञ्जरः, वसुधा, अशनिः.
questions.answer: अम्भोदः = cloud ('water-giver'); तडित् = lightning; कुञ्जरः = elephant; वसुधा = the earth; अशनिः = thunderbolt.
questions.explanation: All five occur in the chapter's verses.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: शीकरः, मर्दलः, केकारवः, सस्यम्, अद्रिः.
questions.answer: शीकरः = fine water-spray/drizzle; मर्दलः = a drum; केकारवः = the peacock's cry; सस्यम् = crop/grain; अद्रिः = mountain.
questions.explanation: Senior-secondary vocabulary from the verses and prose.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद and name the sandhi: (a) घनागमः (b) नैतादृशाः (c) तस्मिन्नद्रौ.
questions.answer: (a) घनागमः = घन + आगमः (अ + आ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः). (b) नैतादृशाः = न + एतादृशाः (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धिसन्धिः). (c) तस्मिन्नद्रौ = तस्मिन् + अद्रौ (doubling of final न् after a short vowel before a vowel — ङमुडागमसन्धिः).
questions.explanation: Each split carries one mark; naming the sandhi type completes the answer.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद: (a) समागतः (b) शापेनास्तंगमितमहिमा (c) सर्वेऽपि.
questions.answer: (a) समागतः = सम् + आगतः. (b) शापेनास्तंगमितमहिमा = शापेन + अस्तंगमितमहिमा (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः). (c) सर्वेऽपि = सर्वे + अपि (after ए the following अ is elided and written as avagraha ऽ — पूर्वरूपसन्धिः).
questions.explanation: All three joins occur in the chapter's verses.

questions.question: Give the विग्रह and name the समास: (a) घनागमः (b) जनकतनया.
questions.answer: (a) घनागमः = घनानाम् आगमः ('arrival of the clouds') — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः. (b) जनकतनया = जनकस्य तनया ('the daughter of Janaka', i.e. Sita) — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः.
questions.explanation: Both dissolve with the genitive — hence shashthi-tatpurusha.

questions.question: 'तडित्पताकः' तथा 'अशनिशब्दमर्दलः' — give the विग्रह of each, name the समास, and state whom the compounds describe.
questions.answer: तडित्पताकः = तडित् पताका यस्य सः ('he whose banner is the lightning') — बहुव्रीहिः. अशनिशब्दमर्दलः = अशनेः शब्दः एव मर्दलः यस्य सः ('he whose drum is the crash of thunder') — बहुव्रीहिः. Both describe घनागमः, the monsoon imagined as a king in ऋतुसंहार 2.1.
questions.explanation: बहुव्रीहि compounds point outside themselves — here to the monsoon-king.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (and number where relevant) of: गगने, वृष्टिभिः, आषाढस्य, वसुधाम्, मासान्.
questions.answer: गगने = सप्तमी एकवचन ('in the sky'); वृष्टिभिः = तृतीया बहुवचन ('with showers'); आषाढस्य = षष्ठी एकवचन ('of Ashadha'); वसुधाम् = द्वितीया एकवचन (object, 'the earth'); मासान् = द्वितीया बहुवचन — the accusative of duration of time ('for some months').
questions.explanation: मासान् shows the special use of द्वितीया for duration (कालात्यन्तसंयोग).

questions.question: Identify the कृदन्त suffix in each and give the meaning: नीत्वा, समागतः, प्रेक्षणीयम्, पातुम्, गायन्तः.
questions.answer: नीत्वा — क्त्वा ('having passed/led'); समागतः — क्त ('arrived'); प्रेक्षणीयम् — अनीयर् ('worth beholding'); पातुम् — तुमुन् ('in order to drink'); गायन्तः — शतृ (present participle, 'singing').
questions.explanation: One mark-worth per correctly identified suffix + meaning.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय (prose order) of: 'अम्भोदा बहवो हि सन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैतादृशाः। केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति वसुधां गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा।'
questions.answer: गगने अम्भोदाः बहवः हि सन्ति, (परं) सर्वे अपि न एतादृशाः। केचित् वृष्टिभिः वसुधाम् आर्द्रयन्ति, केचित् (तु) वृथा गर्जन्ति। — In the sky there are indeed many clouds, but not all are alike; some moisten the earth with showers, some thunder in vain.
questions.explanation: Anvaya rearranges verse-order into natural prose order: locative first, subject, verb; then the contrasting pair केचित्...केचित्.

questions.question: Translate into English: (a) मेघाः गर्जन्ति। (b) तडित् चमकति। (c) मयूराः आनन्देन नृत्यन्ति।
questions.answer: (a) The clouds thunder. (b) Lightning flashes. (c) The peacocks dance with joy.
questions.explanation: Simple present-tense sentences from the prose passage.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'कृषकाः प्रसन्नाः सन्तः क्षेत्रेषु हलैः कृषित्वा बीजानि वपन्ति। ते गायन्तः कार्यं कुर्वन्ति।'
questions.answer: The farmers, being delighted, plough in the fields with their ploughs and sow seeds. They do their work singing.
questions.explanation: सन्तः 'being' (present participle), कृषित्वा 'having ploughed' (क्त्वा), गायन्तः 'singing' (शतृ).

questions.question: घनागमः 'कामिजनप्रियः' इति कथम्? (In what way is the monsoon 'dear to lovers'?)
questions.answer: The monsoon — with its cool winds, dark clouds and pattering rain — is by poetic convention the season of love and union; lovers delight in its romantic atmosphere, while for the separated (like the yaksha) it sharpens longing. Hence the monsoon is called कामिजनप्रियः, 'dear to lovers'.
questions.explanation: The convention also explains why the first cloud of Ashadha overwhelms the separated yaksha.

questions.question: How did the cloud that the yaksha saw on the first day of Ashadha look? Explain the comparison used.
questions.answer: The cloud clung to the mountain-ridge (आश्लिष्टसानुम्) and looked lovely like an elephant bent down in butting-play against a bank (वप्रक्रीडापरिणतगजप्रेक्षणीयम्). Just as a sporting elephant lowers its head and shoulders to butt a mound, the dark massed cloud leaned upon the ridge of Ramagiri.
questions.explanation: The elephant-simile is one of the most celebrated images of the Meghaduta.

questions.question: Name the metre of the मेघदूत and its genre, and say why the metre suits the poem's mood.
questions.answer: The मेघदूत is a खण्डकाव्य (short lyric / messenger-poem) composed throughout in the मन्दाक्रान्ता metre — a slow, stately metre of 17 syllables per quarter. Its name means 'slowly approaching', and its long, measured cadence perfectly matches the poem's mood of lingering longing (विप्रलम्भशृङ्गार) and the slow drifting journey of the cloud.
questions.explanation: Metre (मन्दाक्रान्ता), genre (खण्डकाव्य), and the fitness of slow cadence to longing are the three expected points.

questions.question: Write two simple Sanskrit sentences of your own about वर्षा (the rainy season) and give their English meanings.
questions.answer: Sample answer: 1. वर्षाकाले गगनं मेघैः आवृतं भवति। (In the rainy season the sky becomes covered with clouds.) 2. बालकाः वृष्टौ आनन्देन क्रीडन्ति। (Children play joyfully in the rain.) — Any two grammatically correct sentences on the theme are acceptable.
questions.explanation: Assess subject-verb agreement and correct vibhakti; content may vary.

questions.question: Write a short description of the rainy season (वर्षर्तुवर्णनम्) — at least five simple Sanskrit sentences in Devanagari with an English rendering — using the vocabulary of this chapter.
questions.answer:
Sample answer:
वर्षाकालः समागतः। गगने नीलाः मेघाः गर्जन्ति। तडित् क्षणं क्षणं चमकति। महती वृष्टिः भवति, तेन वसुधा हरिता जाता। वनेषु मयूराः केकारवं कृत्वा नृत्यन्ति। नद्यः जलपूर्णाः भूत्वा वेगेन वहन्ति। कृषकाः प्रसन्नाः क्षेत्रेषु बीजानि वपन्ति।
English: The rainy season has arrived. Dark clouds thunder in the sky. Lightning flashes moment by moment. Heavy rain falls, and by it the earth has turned green. In the forests the peacocks cry and dance. The rivers, becoming full, flow swiftly. The delighted farmers sow seeds in their fields.
Any grammatically correct set of five or more thematic sentences earns full marks.
questions.explanation: Assess correct subject-verb agreement, vibhakti usage and thematic vocabulary (मेघ, तडित्, मयूर, नदी, कृषक).

questions.question: Explain ऋतुसंहार 2.1 ('ससीकराम्भोधरमत्तकुञ्जरः...') in full: give the अन्वय, the meaning, and analyse the poetic device that structures the verse.
questions.answer:
अन्वयः: प्रिये! ससीकर-अम्भोधर-मत्तकुञ्जरः तडित्पताकः अशनिशब्दमर्दलः उद्धतद्युतिः कामिजनप्रियः घनागमः राजवत् समागतः।
Meaning: 'O beloved! The monsoon has arrived like a king in proud splendour — the spray-laden clouds are his rutting elephants, the lightning his banner, the thunder-crash his drum; and he is dear to lovers.'
Analysis: The verse is built on a single sustained उपमा (राजवत्, 'like a king'), worked out limb by limb through बहुव्रीहि compounds: the king's elephants = the clouds; his banner = the lightning (तडित्पताकः); his drum = the thunder (अशनिशब्दमर्दलः); his royal splendour = उद्धतद्युतिः. Each compound describes घनागमः, so the grammar itself carries the picture — a hallmark of Kalidasa's descriptive style. The address प्रिये and the epithet कामिजनप्रियः tie the royal image to the monsoon's conventional role as the season of love.
questions.explanation: Full marks need the anvaya, a faithful translation, and the identification of the sustained simile carried by bahuvrihi compounds.

questions.question: Narrate the opening situation of the मेघदूत (verses 1-2): who is the hero, why is he at Ramagiri, what is his condition, and what does he see on the first day of Ashadha?
questions.answer: The hero is a yaksha, an attendant of Kubera, lord of wealth. Having been negligent in his appointed duty (स्वाधिकारात् प्रमत्तः), he was cursed by his master to lose his powers and glory (अस्तंगमितमहिमा) and to spend one full year (वर्षभोग्येण शापेन) in exile — a curse made crushing because it parted him from his beloved wife (कान्ताविरहगुरुणा). He settled among the hermitages of Mount Ramagiri, whose waters were hallowed by Sita's bathing (जनकतनयास्नानपुण्योदकेषु) and whose trees gave dense shade. There he passed some months, so wasted by grief that his golden bracelet slipped from his bare forearm (कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः). Then, on the first day of आषाढ — the traditional onset of the monsoon — he saw a cloud embracing the mountain-ridge (आश्लिष्टसानुम्), beautiful as an elephant bent down in butting-play against a bank. That sight, which stirs longing even in happy hearts, overwhelmed the separated lover, and he resolved to make the cloud his messenger to his wife in distant Alaka — thus the whole poem is born from this monsoon moment.
questions.explanation: Cover: the yaksha and Kubera, the curse and its cause, Ramagiri and its Sita association, the wasted bracelet-slipping condition, and the Ashadha cloud with its elephant simile.

questions.question: 'रे रे चातक...' — explain the whole verse, define अन्योक्ति, show how the allegory works term by term, and evaluate its relevance today.
questions.answer:
Meaning: 'O chataka, my friend, listen attentively a moment: many clouds are in the sky, but not all are alike — some moisten the earth with showers, others merely thunder in vain; so do not utter piteous words before every one you see.'
अन्योक्तिः is the figure of 'speaking about another': the poet ostensibly addresses a bird, tree or cloud, but the real target is human conduct.
The allegory: the chataka (who by कविसमय drinks only raindrops) = the needy person who must ask for help; the raining clouds = the truly generous, who give quietly; the vainly thundering clouds = boasters who promise loudly and give nothing; the 'piteous words' (दीनं वचः) = begging that costs one's self-respect.
Relevance today: The verse teaches discrimination and dignity — judge people (sponsors, leaders, friends) by their deeds rather than their announcements, seek help selectively, and do not cheapen yourself by pleading before everyone. In an age of loud promises and advertisement, the distinction between those who 'rain' and those who merely 'thunder' remains sharply relevant.
questions.explanation: Four expected components: literal meaning, definition of anyokti, term-by-term mapping, and a reasoned modern evaluation.

questions.question: Write an essay on ऋतुवर्णन (season-description) in Sanskrit kavya, with special reference to Kalidasa's treatment of वर्षा.
questions.answer: Sanskrit poetics counts प्रकृतिवर्णन — descriptions of mountains, rivers, sunrise, and the seasons — among the standard ornaments of a kavya, and poets lavished their finest art upon it. The year's six seasons (वसन्त, ग्रीष्म, वर्षा, शरद्, हेमन्त, शिशिर) each carry conventional imagery, but वर्षा is the poets' favourite: dark thundering clouds, lightning, dancing peacocks, the pleading chataka, brimming rivers and the joy of farmers. Kalidasa is the master of this tradition. His ऋतुसंहारम् devotes a canto to each season; the second canto welcomes the monsoon like a king — clouds for elephants, lightning for banner, thunder for drum (ससीकराम्भोधर...). His मेघदूतम्, a खण्डकाव्य in the मन्दाक्रान्ता metre, turns a single monsoon cloud seen on the first day of आषाढ into the messenger of an exiled yaksha's love — proof that in kavya the monsoon is not scenery but a living actor that stirs emotion (विप्रलम्भशृङ्गार). Later poets and the subhashita tradition continued this love of the rains, as in the chataka-अन्योक्ति where clouds that rain and clouds that merely thunder become images of the generous and the boastful. Thus ऋतुवर्णन unites close observation of nature with feeling and moral reflection — the very essence of Sanskrit poetry.
questions.explanation: Expect: the convention of nature/season description, the six seasons, varsha's imagery, Ritusamhara canto 2, Meghaduta's monsoon frame, and the continuing subhashita tradition.

questions.question: 'In वर्णन-poetry the compounds carry the picture.' Discuss with reference to the समासs of this chapter — give the विग्रह and type of at least four compounds and show what each contributes.
questions.answer: Descriptive poetry packs whole images into single compounds. (1) तडित्पताकः = तडित् पताका यस्य सः (बहुव्रीहि): one word makes the lightning the monsoon-king's banner. (2) अशनिशब्दमर्दलः = अशनेः शब्दः एव मर्दलः यस्य सः (बहुव्रीहि): the thunder-crash becomes his drum — together these two compounds paint the entire royal procession of ऋतुसंहार 2.1. (3) घनागमः = घनानाम् आगमः (षष्ठीतत्पुरुष): the season itself is named by a compound, 'the coming of the clouds'. (4) जनकतनयास्नानपुण्योदकेषु (containing जनकस्य तनया, षष्ठीतत्पुरुष, within a larger बहुव्रीहि): 'whose waters were made holy by Sita's bathing' — a whole sacred history of Ramagiri in one word. (5) कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः (बहुव्रीहि): 'whose forearm was bared by the slipping of the golden bracelet' — the yaksha's wasting grief conveyed without a single direct statement. Because बहुव्रीहि compounds describe something outside themselves, they let the poet heap qualities upon the monsoon or the yaksha swiftly and suggestively; the grammar itself does the describing — which is why mastering समास is the key to reading kavya.
questions.explanation: Any four compounds with correct vigraha, correct type, and a comment on the poetic effect earn full marks.

questions.question: From the sentence 'अबलाविप्रयुक्तः सः कामी तस्मिन् अद्रौ कतिचित् मासान् नीत्वा आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे आश्लिष्टसानुं मेघं ददर्श' — identify (a) all case forms with their विभक्ति and role, (b) all कृदन्त forms with their suffixes, and (c) the tense/लकार of ददर्श.
questions.answer:
(a) Case forms: सः कामी, अबलाविप्रयुक्तः = प्रथमा (subject and its adjectives); तस्मिन् अद्रौ = सप्तमी ('on that mountain'); कतिचित् मासान् = द्वितीया बहुवचन of duration ('for some months'); आषाढस्य = षष्ठी ('of Ashadha'); प्रथमदिवसे = सप्तमी ('on the first day'); आश्लिष्टसानुम् मेघम् = द्वितीया (object and its adjective).
(b) कृदन्त forms: नीत्वा = क्त्वा ('having passed'); विप्रयुक्तः and आश्लिष्ट- = क्त (past participles 'separated', 'embraced').
(c) ददर्श = लिट् लकार (the reduplicated perfect) of दृश्, third person singular — 'he saw'; the classic remote-past narrative tense of kavya.
questions.explanation: A complete parsing exercise: nominatives, locatives, the accusative of duration, genitive, object; krt suffixes; and the perfect tense.

questions.question: Translate the prose passage 'वर्षाकालः समागतः। ... सर्वा प्रकृतिः नवजीवनं प्राप्नोति।' into good English, and then add two Sanskrit sentences of your own continuing the description.
questions.answer:
Translation: The rainy season has arrived. Everywhere in the sky dark clouds thunder; lightning flashes moment by moment; a cool wind blows; heavy rain falls. With the rain-water the earth has turned green. In the forests the peacocks, uttering their cry, dance with joy. The chataka birds gaze at the sky to drink the raindrops. The rivers, becoming full of water, flow swiftly; ponds and wells fill with water. The delighted farmers plough their fields and sow seeds; they work singing. Children play in the rain. All nature receives new life.
Sample continuation: 1. वृक्षाः नवपल्लवैः शोभन्ते। (The trees shine with new leaves.) 2. सर्वे जनाः शीतलं वायुं सेवन्ते। (All the people enjoy the cool breeze.) — Any two correct thematic sentences are acceptable.
questions.explanation: Assess fidelity of the translation and grammatical correctness of the two original sentences.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
ससीकराम्भोधरमत्तकुञ्जरस्तडित्पताकोऽशनिशब्दमर्दलः।
समागतो राजवदुद्धतद्युतिर्घनागमः कामिजनप्रियः प्रिये॥
(a) घनागमः कः इव समागतः? (b) मेघाः किं कल्पिताः? (c) तडित् किं कल्पिता? (d) अशनिशब्दः किं कल्पितः?
questions.answer: (a) घनागमः राजा इव (राजवत्) समागतः — the monsoon arrived like a king. (b) The spray-laden clouds are imagined as his rutting elephants (मत्तकुञ्जराः). (c) The lightning is imagined as his banner (पताका). (d) The crash of thunder is imagined as his drum (मर्दलः).
questions.explanation: Ritusamhara 2.1: each part of the royal procession maps onto one element of the monsoon.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
कश्चित्कान्ताविरहगुरुणा स्वाधिकारात्प्रमत्तः शापेनास्तंगमितमहिमा वर्षभोग्येण भर्तुः।
यक्षश्चक्रे जनकतनयास्नानपुण्योदकेषु स्निग्धच्छायातरुषु वसतिं रामगिर्याश्रमेषु॥
(a) यक्षः कस्मात् शप्तः? (b) शापः कियत्कालं भोग्यः? (c) 'जनकतनया' का? (d) यक्षः कुत्र अवसत्?
questions.answer: (a) He was cursed because he was negligent in his own duty (स्वाधिकारात् प्रमत्तः). (b) The curse was to be endured for one year (वर्षभोग्येण). (c) जनकतनया = the daughter of Janaka, i.e. Sita, whose bathing sanctified the waters of Ramagiri. (d) He dwelt in the hermitages of Mount Ramagiri (रामगिर्याश्रमेषु), amid trees of dense shade.
questions.explanation: Meghaduta 1 — the opening frame of the poem.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
तस्मिन्नद्रौ कतिचिदबलाविप्रयुक्तः स कामी नीत्वा मासान्कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः।
आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे मेघमाश्लिष्टसानुं वप्रक्रीडापरिणतगजप्रेक्षणीयं ददर्श॥
(a) यक्षः कति मासान् तत्र नीतवान्? (b) तस्य प्रकोष्ठः कथं रिक्तः? (c) सः कदा मेघं ददर्श? (d) मेघः कीदृशः प्रेक्षणीयः आसीत्?
questions.answer: (a) He passed 'some' months there (कतिचित् मासान्). (b) His forearm was left bare because his golden bracelet slipped off — grief had made him thin (कनकवलयभ्रंशरिक्तप्रकोष्ठः). (c) He saw the cloud on the first day of Ashadha (आषाढस्य प्रथमदिवसे). (d) The cloud, embracing the ridge, was lovely to behold like an elephant bent down in butting-play against a bank (वप्रक्रीडापरिणतगजप्रेक्षणीयम्).
questions.explanation: Meghaduta 2 — the famous first sight of the monsoon cloud.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
रे रे चातक सावधानमनसा मित्र क्षणं श्रूयतां
अम्भोदा बहवो हि सन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैतादृशाः।
केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति वसुधां गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा
यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः॥
(a) कविः कं सम्बोधयति? (b) के मेघाः वसुधाम् आर्द्रयन्ति? (c) कविः चातकं किं न कर्तुं वदति? (d) अस्मिन् पद्ये कः अलङ्कारः, तस्य लक्ष्यं च किम्?
questions.answer: (a) The poet addresses the chataka bird ('रे रे चातक... मित्र'). (b) Only SOME clouds (केचित्) moisten the earth with their showers; others merely thunder in vain. (c) He tells the bird not to utter piteous words (दीनं वचः मा ब्रूहि) before every cloud it sees. (d) The figure is अन्योक्तिः — through the bird the poet really addresses human beings: beg only from the truly generous, not from every boaster.
questions.explanation: Comprehension plus identification of the allegorical device and its target.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer in Sanskrit:
वर्षाकालः समागतः। गगने नीलाः मेघाः गर्जन्ति। वनेषु मयूराः केकारवं कृत्वा नृत्यन्ति। नद्यः जलपूर्णाः भूत्वा वेगेन वहन्ति। बालकाः वृष्टौ क्रीडन्ति।
(a) गगने के गर्जन्ति? (b) मयूराः किं कृत्वा नृत्यन्ति? (c) नद्यः कथं वहन्ति? (d) बालकाः कुत्र क्रीडन्ति?
questions.answer: (a) गगने नीलाः मेघाः गर्जन्ति। (b) मयूराः केकारवं कृत्वा नृत्यन्ति। (c) नद्यः जलपूर्णाः भूत्वा वेगेन वहन्ति। (d) बालकाः वृष्टौ क्रीडन्ति।
questions.explanation: Direct Sanskrit comprehension: each answer restates the relevant sentence of the passage.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
कृषकाः प्रसन्नाः सन्तः क्षेत्रेषु हलैः कृषित्वा बीजानि वपन्ति। ते गायन्तः कार्यं कुर्वन्ति। सर्वा प्रकृतिः नवजीवनं प्राप्नोति। अतः कवयः वर्षर्तुं 'जीवनदाता' इति वदन्ति।
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of: हलैः, बीजानि, गायन्तः. (b) Why do the poets call the rainy season 'जीवनदाता'?
questions.answer: (a) हलैः = with ploughs (instrumental plural of हल); बीजानि = seeds; गायन्तः = singing (present participle). (b) Because the rains give new life (नवजीवनम्) to all nature — the earth turns green, rivers and wells fill, and the farmers' crops can grow — the poets call वर्षा 'the giver of life'.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary plus a comprehension inference from the passage.

questions.question:
The following joined forms occur in the chapter's verses: घनागमः, नैतादृशाः, सर्वेऽपि, तस्मिन्नद्रौ.
For each: (a) give the सन्धि-विच्छेद and (b) name the sandhi.
questions.answer: घनागमः = घन + आगमः — दीर्घसन्धिः (अ + आ = आ). नैतादृशाः = न + एतादृशाः — वृद्धिसन्धिः (अ + ए = ऐ). सर्वेऽपि = सर्वे + अपि — पूर्वरूपसन्धिः (the अ after ए is elided and written as avagraha ऽ). तस्मिन्नद्रौ = तस्मिन् + अद्रौ — ङमुडागमसन्धिः (final न् after a short vowel doubles before a vowel).
questions.explanation: One split + one name per form; all four occur in the chapter.

questions.question:
Read the sentence and answer:
'चातकाः वृष्टिजलं पातुं गगनं पश्यन्ति। कृषकाः हलैः कृषित्वा बीजानि वपन्ति। ते गायन्तः कार्यं कुर्वन्ति।'
(a) Identify the कृदन्त form meaning 'in order to drink' and name its suffix. (b) Identify the क्त्वा form and give its meaning. (c) State the विभक्ति of हलैः. (d) Identify the शतृ (present participle) form.
questions.answer: (a) पातुम् — formed with the तुमुन् suffix, 'in order to drink'. (b) कृषित्वा — 'having ploughed' (क्त्वा suffix). (c) हलैः = तृतीया बहुवचन, 'with ploughs'. (d) गायन्तः — 'singing', the शतृ present participle (masculine plural).
questions.explanation: A grammar-spotting exercise on the prose passage.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
'The Indian year is divided into six seasons of two months each. Poets found in each season its own imagery, but the rains inspired them most: Kalidasa devoted the second canto of his Ritusamhara to varsha, and his Meghaduta begins with a monsoon cloud seen on the first day of Ashadha.'
(a) How many seasons are there and of how many months each? (b) Which canto of the Ritusamhara describes varsha? (c) With what monsoon event does the Meghaduta begin?
questions.answer: (a) Six seasons (षड् ऋतवः), of two months each. (b) The second canto of the ऋतुसंहार describes वर्षा. (c) The मेघदूत begins with the exiled yaksha seeing a cloud embracing the ridge of Ramagiri on the first day of the month आषाढ.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the chapter's account of the ritu-varnana tradition.

questions.question:
Read the lines and answer:
'वनेषु मयूराः केकारवं कृत्वा आनन्देन नृत्यन्ति। चातकाः वृष्टिजलं पातुं गगनं पश्यन्ति। तडागाः कूपाः च जलेन पूर्णाः भवन्ति।'
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of: केकारवम्, चातकाः, तडागाः, कूपाः. (b) Which two birds of the rainy season are mentioned, and what does each do?
questions.answer: (a) केकारवम् = the cry of the peacock; चातकाः = chataka birds; तडागाः = ponds; कूपाः = wells. (b) The peacock (मयूरः), which utters its cry and dances with joy; and the chataka, which watches the sky to drink the falling rain-water.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary and comprehension from the prose passage.
